nodes.name: Fetch Bitrix deals
nodes.notes:
DEAL_FIELD_ALLOWLIST, verbatim from sources/bitrix_chats.py. Only deals modified in the last 7 days: the CRM holds 2,496 and re-reading all of them nightly buys nothing.

UNVERIFIED AGAINST THE PORTAL. bitrix_chats.py says so in writing for the imopenlines methods; crm.deal.list is the best documented of the set but has still never been called against cultiv.bitrix24.com. Run the probe before trusting a run.

parameters.query:
-- Bitrix deals, pulled instead of exported by hand.
--
-- WHAT THIS REPLACES. A human exported DEAL_*.csv from the CRM, copied it to a
-- laptop, opened a Railway tunnel and ran import_bitrix_phones.py. That is a
-- snapshot with a date on it: re-running it a month later knows nothing about
-- anything that happened since, and between exports every new conversation is
-- an island with no customer to belong to.
--
-- ONLY THE ALLOWLISTED FIELDS. The deal object carries UF_CRM_1781281581, which
-- contains prose addressed to a bot, and a dozen fields holding another
-- system's AI verdicts on lead temperature and intent -- the exact judgements
-- this project exists to produce from the conversation itself, with evidence.
-- Importing somebody else's unverifiable version of them puts two disagreeing
-- answers in one database with nothing to say which is which.
INSERT INTO deals (
  bitrix_deal_id, title, category_id, stage_id, stage_semantic, is_closed,
  amount, currency, created_at_src, modified_at_src, begin_date, close_date,
  origin)
SELECT d->>'ID', d->>'TITLE', d->>'CATEGORY_ID', d->>'STAGE_ID',
       left(coalesce(d->>'STAGE_SEMANTIC_ID', ''), 1),
       (d->>'CLOSED') = 'Y',
       nullif(d->>'OPPORTUNITY', '')::numeric,
       nullif(d->>'CURRENCY_ID', ''),
       nullif(d->>'DATE_CREATE', '')::timestamptz,
       nullif(d->>'DATE_MODIFY', '')::timestamptz,
       nullif(d->>'BEGINDATE', '')::date,
       nullif(d->>'CLOSEDATE', '')::date,
       'bitrix_rest'
FROM jsonb_array_elements($1::jsonb) AS d
WHERE d->>'ID' IS NOT NULL
ON CONFLICT (bitrix_deal_id) DO UPDATE SET
  title           = EXCLUDED.title,
  stage_id        = EXCLUDED.stage_id,
  stage_semantic  = EXCLUDED.stage_semantic,
  is_closed       = EXCLUDED.is_closed,
  -- NEVER overwrite an amount a human typed. is_manual_amount marks those, and
  -- the CRM's own number losing to it is the whole point of that flag.
  amount          = CASE WHEN deals.is_manual_amount THEN deals.amount
                         ELSE EXCLUDED.amount END,
  currency        = EXCLUDED.currency,
  modified_at_src = EXCLUDED.modified_at_src,
  close_date      = EXCLUDED.close_date,
  updated_at      = now()
RETURNING deal_id, bitrix_deal_id, stage_id;

-- Link conversations to the deals that now exist, and nothing else.
--
-- 01c deliberately does not create a stub deal, so a thread that arrived before
-- its deal was pulled carries external_deal_id and a NULL FK. This closes that
-- gap once the deal is really there.
--
-- NEVER OVERWRITES: only rows where deal_id IS NULL are touched.
UPDATE interactions i
   SET deal_id = d.deal_id, updated_at = now()
  FROM deals d
 WHERE d.bitrix_deal_id = i.external_deal_id
   AND i.deal_id IS NULL
RETURNING i.interaction_id, d.bitrix_deal_id;

-- Retention. Raw customer words older than the window are deleted; every
-- conclusion drawn from them, and the id needed to fetch them again from
-- Bitrix or Drive, is kept forever.
--
-- CHAT AND CALL WINDOWS DIFFER ON PURPOSE. Bitrix still holds the chat text,
-- so 90 days is recoverable. A call recording is not reliably recoverable: if
-- Drive's own retention deletes the WAV after we deleted our transcript, that
-- conversation is gone from the world. Call text therefore keeps a year, which
-- costs 0.14 GB.
--
-- The rule lives in purge_raw_content (017), not here, so a backfill and this
-- node can never disagree about what "old" means.
SELECT * FROM purge_raw_content(90, 365, false);

-- Did anything actually get judged today, and what has it cost?
--
-- WHY THIS EXISTS. Chat threads were stored for six days without a single one
-- being evaluated and nobody noticed -- 01d was simply switched off. Storage
-- succeeding while scoring silently does nothing is the failure this pipeline
-- is most prone to, because every dashboard keeps rendering the older numbers
-- and looks healthy.
--
-- A row with detail->>'alert' = true is the signal. It is deliberately a ROW
-- and not an exception: a workflow that throws stops, and a nightly job that
-- stops is one more thing that fails quietly.
WITH last24 AS (
  SELECT
    (SELECT count(*) FROM agent_evaluations WHERE created_at > now() - interval '24 hours') AS evaluations,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM chat_messages     WHERE created_at > now() - interval '24 hours') AS messages_in,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM transcripts       WHERE transcribed_at > now() - interval '24 hours') AS transcripts_in,
    (SELECT count(*) FROM chat_eval_jobs    WHERE status IN ('pending','judge_failed')) AS queue,
    (SELECT coalesce(sum(cost_usd), 0) FROM model_calls WHERE created_at > now() - interval '24 hours') AS spend_24h,
    (SELECT coalesce(sum(cost_usd), 0) FROM model_calls WHERE created_at > date_trunc('month', now())) AS spend_month
)
INSERT INTO job_runs (job_name, started_at, finished_at, status, items_in, items_ok, cost_usd, detail)
SELECT 'nightly_health', now(), now(),
       CASE WHEN evaluations = 0 AND messages_in > 0 THEN 'failed' ELSE 'succeeded' END,
       messages_in, evaluations, spend_month,
       jsonb_build_object(
         'evaluations_24h', evaluations,
         'messages_24h',    messages_in,
         'transcripts_24h', transcripts_in,
         'queue_depth',     queue,
         'spend_24h_usd',   spend_24h,
         'spend_month_usd', spend_month,
         -- The budget guard. Crossing it does not stop anything by itself; it
         -- puts a visible row in job_runs, which is what a human acts on.
         'over_budget',     spend_month > 40,
         'alert',           (evaluations = 0 AND messages_in > 0) OR spend_month > 40)
FROM last24
RETURNING run_id, job_name, status, detail;

-- Which contacts do we still have no phone for?
--
-- Bounded on purpose. crm.contact.list takes a filter, not the whole address
-- book, and 500 ids is already more than a night's worth of new conversations.
-- Anything left over is picked up tomorrow.
SELECT jsonb_agg(DISTINCT external_contact_id) AS contact_ids,
       count(DISTINCT external_contact_id)     AS n
FROM (
  SELECT external_contact_id
  FROM interactions
  WHERE external_contact_id IS NOT NULL
    AND customer_phone_e164 IS NULL
  LIMIT 500
) s;

nodes.name: Fetch Bitrix contacts
nodes.notes: ID and PHONE only. A contact record also carries name, email and assorted UF_ fields; none of them is needed to link a conversation to a person, and every one of them would be personal data stored for no stated purpose.

nodes.name: Normalise phones
nodes.notes: DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION=SA is a DECISION, not a format: 0500000000 is a valid Saudi mobile and meaningless in Egypt. A bare Egyptian number fails here rather than being assigned +966 — a null phone is recoverable, a wrong-country match merges two real people. The rule lives in the worker; this asks it instead of keeping a second copy in SQL.

parameters.query:
-- Write the normalised phone onto every conversation of that contact.
--
-- ZIPPED BY POSITION. The worker returns one result per value, in the order it
-- received them, so ordinality is the join key. That is only safe because the
-- pairing node builds both arrays in one pass -- if either list is ever built
-- separately, this join silently pairs the wrong phone with the wrong person.
--
-- NEVER OVERWRITES. Only rows where customer_phone_e164 IS NULL are touched: a
-- phone already there came from the source that owns the conversation, and a
-- nightly CRM sweep does not get to overrule it.
--
-- NULLS ARE SKIPPED, NOT WRITTEN. A number that failed to normalise (a bare
-- Egyptian mobile, say) leaves the row untouched and eligible tomorrow, rather
-- than being stamped with a wrong-country guess that would merge two people.
WITH pairs AS (
  SELECT ordinality AS o, value->>'contact_id' AS cid
  FROM jsonb_array_elements($1::jsonb) WITH ORDINALITY AS t(value, ordinality)
), norm AS (
  SELECT ordinality AS o, value->>'e164' AS e164
  FROM jsonb_array_elements($2::jsonb) WITH ORDINALITY AS t(value, ordinality)
)
UPDATE interactions i
   SET customer_phone_e164 = n.e164,
       updated_at = now()
  FROM pairs p
  JOIN norm n ON n.o = p.o
 WHERE i.external_contact_id = p.cid
   AND i.customer_phone_e164 IS NULL
   AND n.e164 IS NOT NULL
RETURNING i.interaction_id, i.external_contact_id, i.customer_phone_e164;
